create.name: Mícheál Ó Súilleabháin
create.bio:
Known to friends as Moley, Mícheál Ó Súilleabháin is an Irish poet, singer and speaker. He grew up in Limerick in a household full of traditional music and scholarship. He began as a drummer, read music at University College Cork and took a master's in ethnomusicology at the Irish World Academy, then spent years teaching rap and vocal percussion to young people. In his twenties he set out to learn the old songs carried by his mother, the singer and theologian Nóirín Ní Riain, and the two of them, with his brother Owen, went on to sing together as a trio in Europe and North America.

With Owen and Nóirín he leads Turas d'Anam, Irish for 'journey of your soul': week-long journeys in Kerry and Cork that mix morning sessions of song, story, poetry and myth with visits to stone circles and pilgrimage sites, and the Inner Soul Circle, an online community that follows the Celtic year with monthly letters, recorded talks and live gatherings. The brothers also teach together at retreat centres such as Kripalu, often on Celtic spirituality and the figure of St Patrick, and have taught alongside the poet David Whyte, whose Many Rivers Press published Mícheál's first poetry collection, Early Music.

courses.title: The Celtic Wisdom of Connection
courses.description: A weekend at Kripalu with Mícheál and his brother Owen, built around Irish poetry, song and the story of St Patrick. They look at how Celtic and Christian spirituality met in Ireland, with plenty of singing and recitation along the way.

courses.title: The Rebel County Journey: Journey to the Unique Genius of Ireland
courses.description: A week in County Cork led by the two brothers and their mother, starting each day with song, story and poetry before heading out to ancient sites and meeting local musicians and artists. The theme is independence and finding one's own rebel spirit. Private room, most meals and in-country transport are included; flights are not.

courses.title: The Kingdom County Journey: Journey to the West Coast of Ireland
courses.description: A week based at Parknasilla in County Kerry, exploring the Atlantic coast with the family as lecturers, singers and workshop leaders. Mornings of myth and music lead into outings to stone circles, holy places and Irish cultural figures. Private room, most meals and local transport are included; flights are not.

courses.title: Inner Soul Circle
courses.description: An online membership that moves through the Celtic calendar month by month. Members receive a seasonal letter, a recorded talk and a live Zoom gathering with the three teachers, with recordings kept for those who miss it.

flags: Pair listing: the queue marks him as teaching with his brother Owen Ó Súilleabháin (they lead the Kripalu programme together, share a Facebook page, Instagram and YouTube channel, and run Turas d'Anam with their mother Nóirín Ní Riain). One listing under Mícheál's name, since he is the queue entry and has his own site; Owen and Nóirín are in the bio. Owner may prefer a pair name such as 'Owen and Mícheál Ó Súilleabháin'.

Name clash risk: his late father, the composer Mícheál Ó Súilleabháin (1950–2018), is far better known online under the same name; check no existing listing or search confusion. He also goes by 'Moley'.
Name spelling: the queue has 'Míchéál'; Kripalu and his own site use 'Mícheál', which is used here (slug unchanged).
Mostly a poet and singer: kept because his Kripalu, Turas d'Anam and Inner Soul Circle work teaches Celtic spirituality, but a human may judge this closer to a music/arts listing.
Videos come from the brothers' shared channel and the Turas d'Anam family channel; Mícheál is one of two or three speakers in most. Two are spoken poems rather than talks.
Availability worldwide: he lives in Killaloe, Co. Clare (X bio) and leads tours in Kerry and Cork, but has no fixed place where he holds classes.
Kripalu programme copy frames Irish wisdom as 'medicine' and 'a cure for our postmodern age' (metaphor, not a health claim); not used in the description.
The Turas d'Anam brand inbox turasdanam@gmail.com is also published (contact page); his personal published address is used instead.
